product.olivetti-m19.summary: Olivetti’s compact entry-level PC whose system unit drew power from the monochrome monitor.
product.olivetti-m19.history: The M19 appears in an Olivetti brochure printed in March 1986 for beginners, classrooms and affordable networked workstations. It occupied the entry level of the professional range, with a much lower case than conventional PCs. Practical Computing quoted a British price of £1,306 for the basic configuration in June 1986. Acorn also marketed an M19, advertised for education, training and business in July 1986. Sources: Olivetti, code 39552; Glyn Moody, Practical Computing, pp. 48–49; Acorn, APP 86.
product.olivetti-m19.warning: Historical sheet under research: BluMach contains an M19 implementation, with no boot validation performed for this sheet.
product.olivetti-m19.technical.cpu: The dual-speed kit made the machine faster. The brochures document a 4.77 MHz 8088, upgradable to 8 MHz with DSK 1921, and 256 KB RAM expandable to 640 KB on the motherboard; the data bus was 8-bit.
product.olivetti-m19.technical.expansion: The small case shaped expansion options. The Italian brochure distinguishes two internal connectors for proprietary cards and an external box for one standard card: EXB 1940 or EXB 1941. These are not three equivalent internal ISA slots.
product.olivetti-m19.technical.power: The monitor was part of the power arrangement. Practical Computing describes the supply inside the monochrome monitor; the Italian brochure offers the powered EXB 1941 for using the computer with a colour monitor.
product.olivetti-m19.technical.video: Integrated video went beyond basic CGA. The Italian brochure documents 640 × 400 monochrome and Plantronics modes of 320 × 200 with 16 colours or 640 × 200 with 4 colours, alongside standard modes.
product.olivetti-m19.technical.storage: Advertised disks varied by offering. The March 1986 Italian brochure offers 10 MB with a SCSI controller; the February 1987 German brochure offers 20 MB, also SCSI. Both document 5.25-inch, 360 KB floppy drives. Identical geometry is not assumed.
product.olivetti-m19.technical.firmware: The implementation needs specific BIOS and character ROMs. The m19 loader requests Resident Diagnostics Rev 3.71, 16 KiB at FC000h, and the character ROM identified by the PCF3 filename. These are code metadata, not a certified local ROM set.
product.olivetti-m19.technical.verified: The model’s presence in the code has been checked. M19 appears in 86Box 6a43d7973 and BluMach 88f74ba3. The current table allows 4.773 to 7.159 MHz, compared with the 4.77 and 8 MHz advertised in the brochures; this difference remains to be investigated.
product.olivetti-m19.technical.limitatio: The sheet does not yet allow machine creation. Code comments report limitations in 640 × 400, the optional mouse and the timer at 4.77 MHz; these have not been reproduced here. Firmware with verified provenance and boot, video, storage and reset tests remain pending.
product.olivetti-m19.technical.source_it: Olivetti, Caratteristiche tecniche Personal Computer M19, code 39552, printing 3-86, four pages: audience, CPU, memory, expansion, video and 10 MB SCSI. Preserved from the University of Pisa.
product.olivetti-m19.technical.source_de: Deutsche Olivetti, Personal Computer M19, Hardware-Informationen, 04/071/M19/2.87, four pages: German configuration and 20 MB SCSI. Preserved from Olivrea.
product.olivetti-m19.technical.source_pr: Glyn Moody, “The Great and the Small”, Practical Computing, June 1986, pp. 48–49: market position, power arrangement and British price of £1,306. This is not a universal price, and its tax treatment is not assumed.
product.olivetti-m19.technical.source_ac: Acorn Computers, Acorn Personal Computer M19, APP 86, first edition July 1986, six pages: Acorn sales, configurations and optional Econet. It does not prove that all BIOS versions were identical.
product.olivetti-m19.technical.source_co: BluMach 88f74ba3, m_xt_olivetti.c and machine_table.c: loader, video, CPU range and recorded limitations. Implementation evidence, not validated hardware.
product.olivetti-m19.technical.source_fo: 86Box 6a43d7973, m_xt_olivetti.c: earlier presence of the model and recorded limitations. Its support does not certify a local BluMach boot.
product.olivetti-m19.technical.source_ph: Jason Quinn, 8 April 2008, Wikimedia Commons: M19 with expansion box, without monitor or keyboard. Unmodified original photograph, released into the public domain by its author.
